reasoning: Eight metered samples at n=1..8 (23,133,773,477,219,207,752,44 mod 1009) rule out every polynomial model of degree 1-6 and every order-1 recurrence over GF(1009), and are consistent with a unique order-2 constant-coefficient recurrence f(n) = 11*f(n-1) + 979*f(n-2) mod 1009. That fit is overdetermined: 6 equations in 2 unknowns, with all 4 surplus equations satisfied exactly, so it is a measured fit and not an interpolation. Since 979 = -30 mod 1009, the characteristic polynomial is x^2 - 11x + 30 = (x-5)(x-6), and the initial conditions give the closed form f(n) = 5^n + 3*6^n mod 1009. The multiplicative orders are ord(5) = 504 and ord(6) = 252 mod 1009, so f is purely periodic with period 504. The stated domain [1,600] therefore contains a complete period, and the proposition over [1,600] is equivalent to the stronger statement that 163 is not in the image of f at any integer at all. Exhaustive evaluation of the closed form over one full period n in [1,504] (a complete check, not a bounded search: periodicity makes it exhaustive over all n) shows f attains 378 of the 1009 residues and 163 is not among them; the direct scan over n in [1,600] likewise yields no n with f(n) = 163. I then bought 16 further metered samples spread across the domain (n = 12, 25, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, 350, 400, 450, 500, 550, 599, 600, including both endpoints) as an independent test of the closed form far from the fitting window; all 16 agree exactly, for 24/24 total agreement. Stated limitation: the closed form is inferred from 24 observed points out of 600, so a single-point deviation from the recurrence at one of the 576 unobserved points cannot be excluded by observation - excluding it would require testing all 600 points, and the enforced cap is 120 calls, so no route within this budget can rule it out. The verdict rests on the identified algebraic structure, which is confirmed at every point I was able to buy.
route_taken: I spent 8 calls sampling a contiguous prefix to fit an algebraic model rather than scanning the domain, because range(1,600) costs 600 against a 120-call cap and is unaffordable by construction, whereas 8 samples suffice to identify an order-2 recurrence whose 504-periodicity converts a 600-point universal claim into a closed-form question I can settle for free; the remaining 16 calls went to spread-out endpoint-inclusive spot checks of that model rather than to more contiguous coverage, since a sample confirms both the model and the non-163 property at its point while a range call confirms only the latter.
what_would_resolve_it: Only exhaustive metered coverage of all 600 points (600 calls, or range 1 600) would close the residual risk that the sealed sequence departs from f(n) = 5^n + 3*6^n mod 1009 at one of the 576 points I did not observe; that is 5x the enforced 120-call cap. Alternatively, disclosure of the sealed defining coefficients would settle it at zero further cost, since the closed form's periodicity already makes the [1,600] question decidable in full.
